faqs.a: Most interior wall paints cover 8–12 m² per litre per coat — 10 is a safe average for the calculator's default. Check your tin's label: premium paints often claim 12–14 m²/L on smooth, primed walls, while textured walls can drop to 6–8 m²/L.
faqs.q: What coverage value should I use?

faqs.a: Usually two. One coat over a similar colour can work, but colour changes, new plaster, and patches need two coats for an even finish. Dark-to-light changes sometimes need a primer plus two coats.
faqs.q: How many coats do I need?

faqs.a: The 10% covers roller absorption, cutting-in, and spillage. On very textured or porous surfaces, bump it to 15–20% by lowering the coverage value instead — that models the extra paint more honestly.
Only the wall area: 2 × (length + width) × height, minus doors and windows. Ceilings need a separate calculation (length × width) and usually flat white paint, so they are excluded here.
Use the coverage hint on your primer's tin — primers often cover more (12–15 m²/L). Calculate the primer as one coat with its own coverage, then the topcoat separately with this calculator.
faqs.q: How do I calculate primer too?

faqs.a: The greedy breakdown (20L, 10L, 4L, 1L) gives the fewest tins, but shops may not stock every size and bulk tins are cheaper per litre. Treat the suggestion as a starting point and adjust to what your store sells.
faqs.q: Should I buy exactly the suggested cans?

paint-calculator.formula:
Wall area = 2 × (length + width) × height
Paintable area = wall area − (doors × 2.0 m²) − (windows × 1.5 m²)
Litres = paintable area × coats / coverage × 1.10 (10% wastage)

paint-calculator.quickAnswer: A 4 m × 3 m room with 3 m walls has 42 m² of wall; minus one door (2 m²) that is 40 m² to paint. At 2 coats and 10 m²/L coverage: 40 × 2 ÷ 10 = 8 litres, plus 10% wastage = 8.8 litres — so buy a 10 L can, or 2 × 4 L cans. Enter your own room dimensions and the calculator does the rest, including the can breakdown.
paint-calculator.tagline: How many litres of paint does your room need? Wall area, coats, and can sizes — solved.
paint-calculator.workedExample:
Room 4 m × 3 m, walls 3 m high, 1 door, 2 coats, coverage 10 m²/L:
1. Wall area = 2 × (4 + 3) × 3 = 42 m².
2. Minus door: 42 − 2.0 = 40 m² paintable.
3. Litres = 40 × 2 / 10 = 8 L.
4. With 10% wastage: 8 × 1.10 = 8.8 L.
5. Cans: round 8.8 up to 9 L → 2 × 4 L + 1 × 1 L (a single 10 L can also works and is often cheaper per litre).
